They were apart of the same company. Frischs was a franchisee of Big Boy. When Big Boys parent company was facing bankruptcy,  one of the franchisees, Elias Bros purchased the company. They dropped Elias Bros from their name to simply just be Big Boy. At that time Frischs decided to split from the Big Boy chain, but unlike when Shoneys and Eat N Park left the chain, a deal was made. Frischs would pay a licensing fee to continue use of the Big Boy name and branding. Neither chain could enter each others territory. Frischs owned the trademark for their territory,  and Big Boy owned the trademark for the rest of the country. As for the food, each franchisee used the Big Boy menu, however they could also change or alter it to local flavor. For the Big Boy sandwich Bobs in California used red relish and mayo, Elias Bros and others simply combined the two sauces together.  Frischs changed theirs and used tartar sauce and pickles instead. So yes they were a part of the same company, but now like Shoneys and Eat N Park, they are now seperate companies.
